newsitem.title: FRANCE: French military aircraft sent to land near Kabul.
newsitem.headline: French military aircraft sent to land near Kabul.

text.p: France said on Thursday it had sent a military aircraft to land near Kabul in order to help evacuate any foreigners wishing to escape a rebel assault on the Afghan capital.
A French Foreign Ministry spokesman told reporters that the plane was due to stop first at Islamabad in Pakistan on Thursday and fly on to an airstrip north of Kabul.
Out of 30 French nationals in Kabul, about a dozen wished to stay, the spokesman said.

The Afghan government sent fresh troops to frontlines around Kabul to hold off the rebel Taleban militia as the two sides fought on Thursday, ignoring a U.N. Security Council call for an immediate ceasefire.
Kabul city was calm, and shops and markets were open with no visible sign of panic.

At least 20 foreign aid workers were evacuated from Bagram on two flights arranged by the International Committee of the Red Cross on Thursday as Afghan passengers were getting ready to board a flight of the state airline Ariana to the Indian capital of New Delhi.
